title: Induction of labour: Bishop score, prostaglandins, mechanical methods, oxytocin and uterine tachysystole
subject: ss-obg
refs: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 26 (Induction and Augmentation of Labor)
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 107: Induction of Labor

steps.say: Pre-induction assessment of cervical ripeness predicts the likelihood of successful vaginal birth. The modified Bishop scoring system grades cervical dilation, effacement, station, consistency, and position. A score of 6 or less denotes an unfavorable cervix requiring priming, whereas 8 or more predicts high success.
steps.tx: The modified **Bishop score** evaluates pre-induction cervical readiness across 5 components: dilation, effacement, fetal station, cervical consistency, and position. A score of 6 or less indicates an **unfavorable cervix** mandating cervical ripening, whereas a score of 8 or more reflects a ripe cervix favorable for direct induction.

steps.say: Cervical ripening agents alter the extracellular matrix through active collagen breakdown and water uptake. Prostaglandin E2, formulated as intracervical dinoprostone gel or slow-release vaginal inserts, promotes hyaluronic acid synthesis and stromal softening prior to active myometrial stimulation.
steps.tx: Pharmacological cervical ripening employs **dinoprostone** (prostaglandin E2), available as a 0.5 mg **intracervical gel** or 10 mg controlled-release **vaginal insert**, which stimulates local cervical collagenase, elastase, and hyaluronic acid synthesis to break down rigid collagen fibrils and soften the fibromuscular cervical matrix.

rows: Instant retrieval via attached string if tachysystole
Potent, inexpensive; contraindicated in prior uterine scar

steps.say: Misoprostol offers a versatile and cost-effective prostaglandin option for inducing labour in unscarred uteri. Low-dose oral or vaginal administration at 25 micrograms every two to four hours achieves rapid cervical effacement, but remains strictly contraindicated in women with a previous cesarean section scar.
steps.tx: Synthetic prostaglandin E1, **misoprostol**, administered as 25 micrograms orally or vaginally every 2 to 4 hours, provides potent cervical ripening. However, its use is strictly contraindicated in patients with a **previous cesarean section** or transmural myomectomy due to elevated risks of catastrophic **uterine rupture**.

left.title: Misoprostol (PGE1) in Unscarred Uterus
points: Dose: 25 micrograms orally or vaginally every 2 to 4 hours
High efficacy in achieving vaginal birth within 24 hours
Thermally stable, highly cost-effective global agent

right.title: Strict Contraindication in Prior Scar
points: Dramatically increases uterine rupture risk (up to 5-10%)
Uncontrolled myometrial hyperstimulation at scar edge
Mechanical methods preferred for VBAC induction

steps.say: Mechanical methods ripen the cervix by applying physical pressure without inducing systemic pharmacological side effects. Inserting an intracervical Foley catheter balloon inflated with 30 to 60 milliliters of sterile water promotes local endogenous prostaglandin and oxytocin release via Ferguson's reflex.
steps.tx: Mechanical cervical ripening using a **Foley balloon catheter** inflated with 30 to 60 mL of sterile saline exerts direct mechanical pressure on the internal os. This promotes endogenous **prostaglandin release** and deciduocervical separation while completely avoiding the risk of drug-induced **uterine tachysystole**.

nodes.label: Identify unfavorable cervix (Bishop score <= 6) with prior uterine scar
Pass 16-18F Foley catheter through internal os under direct visualization
Inflate balloon with 30 to 60 mL sterile water and apply gentle traction
Achieve spontaneous catheter expulsion with cervical dilation >= 3 cm

steps.say: Intravenous oxytocin is the primary medication used to stimulate rhythmic uterine contractions once the cervix is ripe. Low-dose physiological titration begins at 1 to 2 milliunits per minute, escalating incrementally by 1 to 2 milliunits every 30 minutes until an optimal contraction pattern emerges.
steps.tx: Standard induction with **intravenous oxytocin** utilizes a low-dose protocol starting at 1 to 2 mU/min, escalating by 1 to 2 mU/min every 30 minutes to establish an optimal pattern of 3 to 4 contractions every 10 minutes, minimizing the risk of myocardial receptor desensitization and fluid overload.

steps.say: Artificial rupture of membranes releases high concentrations of local prostaglandins and facilitates direct fetal head descent. When performing amniotomy on a favorable cervix, clinicians must first confirm that the fetal vertex is well-engaged to prevent cord prolapse, and document clear fluid.
steps.tx: **Amniotomy** (artificial rupture of membranes) is performed when the cervix is ripe and the fetal vertex is firmly engaged at station zero or below. It exposes the fetal head to the lower uterine segment, triggering endogenous oxytocin surges while requiring immediate fetal heart auscultation to exclude **umbilical cord prolapse**.

left.title: Amniotomy Indication & Technique
points: Favorable cervix with engaged vertex (station 0 or lower)
Amnihook punctures membranes during contraction peak
Inspect fluid color (clear, blood-tinged, or meconium)

right.title: Critical Safety Hazards
points: Umbilical cord prolapse if vertex is high or unengaged
Vasa previa laceration causing fetal exsanguination
Ascending chorioamnionitis if delivery prolonged > 18-24 hours

steps.say: Excessive uterine stimulation endangers fetal oxygenation by compressing intramyometrial blood vessels. Uterine tachysystole is defined as more than five contractions within a ten-minute window, averaged over thirty minutes, requiring immediate oxytocin discontinuation and lateral maternal repositioning.
steps.tx: **Uterine tachysystole** is defined as more than 5 contractions in 10 minutes, averaged over a 30-minute window, occurring with or without fetal heart decelerations. It mandates immediate cessation of oxytocin infusion, maternal left lateral repositioning, and intravenous hydration to restore intervillous perfusion.

nodes.label: Document > 5 uterine contractions in 10 minutes on tocodynamometry
Position mother in left lateral decubitus and administer 500 mL IV crystalloid bolus
Administer subcutaneous terbutaline 0.25 mg if abnormal fetal heart rate persists

steps.say: Refractory uterine hypertonus with associated fetal heart rate decelerations requires rapid pharmacological tocolysis. Subcutaneous terbutaline at 0.25 milligrams provides prompt myometrial smooth muscle relaxation, restoring placental blood flow and resolving fetal bradycardia.
steps.tx: When uterine tachysystole produces non-reassuring fetal heart rate decelerations unresponsive to conservative positioning and fluid boluses, acute **tocolysis** with subcutaneous **terbutaline** (0.25 mg) relaxes myometrial smooth muscle tone within 2 to 3 minutes, rapidly reversing fetal hypoxemia and avoiding emergency cesarean delivery.
